{{Short description|Mathematician}}
[[File:Mikhail_Borovoi.jpg|thumb]]

'''Mikhail Vol'fovich Borovoi''' ([[Russian language|Russian]]: Михаи́л Во́льфович Борово́й, [[Hebrew language|Hebrew]]: מיכאל בורובוי; born February 17, 1951) is a Soviet and Israeli mathematician.  He has worked on [[Galois cohomology]] and on the arithmetic of [[linear algebraic group|linear algebraic groups]], homogeneous spaces, [[Shimura variety|Shimura varieties]], and [[spherical variety|spherical varieties]].

==Education and career==

Borovoi was born in Moscow.  He obtained his diploma (M.Sc.) in Mathematics at  [[Moscow State University|Lomonosov Moscow State University]], and his Ph.D. at the [[St. Petersburg Department of Steklov Mathematical Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences| Leningrad Department  (now: St. Petersburg Department) of the Steklov Institute of Mathematics]]<ref>{{MathGenealogyProject|id=83825}}</ref> in 1980; his doctoral advisor was [[Arkady Lvovich Onishchik|Arkady L. Onishchik]]. 
Because of [[Antisemitism in the Soviet Union]] of the time, Borovoi could not find a job as a mathematician, and only with the start of [[Perestroika]], in 1987 he got a position of a Senior Researcher 
at the [http://www.iam.khv.ru/index_eng.php Khabarovsk Division of the Institute for Applied Mathematics of the Far Eastern Branch of the USSR Academy of Sciences]<ref name="IAS">[https://www.ias.edu/scholars/mikhail-v-borovoi  Page of Mikhail Borovoi in the List of Scholars of the Institute for Advanced Study]</ref> in the [[Khabarovsk|Far Eastern city of Khabarovsk]]. He spent the 1990-1991 academic year at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref name="IAS" />  Since 1992 he has been at [[Tel Aviv University]],<ref name="IAS" /> where now he is Professor Emeritus.<ref>[https://en-exact-sciences.tau.ac.il/math/professors-emeriti-and-kamea-members  List of Professors Emeriti of the School of Mathematical Sciences, Tel Aviv University]</ref>
==Research==

Borovoi is known for the Borovoi fundamental group<ref>[[Laurent Fargues]] and [[Peter Scholze]], Geometrization of the local Langlands correspondence, https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.13459, p. 90</ref> of a [[reductive group]]. 
Jointly with [[James S. Milne]],<ref> James S. Milne, The action of an automorphism of C on a Shimura variety and its special points. Arithmetic and Geometry, Vol. I, 239-265, Progr. Math., 35, Birkhäuser Boston, Boston, MA, 1983.</ref> Borovoi proved<ref>M. V. Borovoi,
Langlands' conjecture concerning conjugation of connected Shimura varieties. Selecta Math. Soviet. 3 (1983/84), no. 1, 3–39.</ref> Shimura's conjecture
in the theory of [[Shimura variety|Shimura varieties]], which was the subject of Borovoi's invited talk<ref>M. V. Borovoi, Conjugation of Shimura varieties. Proceedings of the
International Congress of Mathematicians, Vol. 1 (Berkeley, Calif.,1986), 783-790, Amer. Math. Soc., Providence, RI, 1987.</ref> at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], Berkeley, 1986.
He proved that the [[Brauer-Manin obstruction]] is the only obstruction to the [[Hasse principle]] and weak approximation for homogeneous spaces of connected
[[linear algebraic group|linear algebraic groups]] over [[number field|number fields]] with connected geometric stabilizers.<ref>Mikhail Borovoi, The Brauer-Manin obstructions for homogeneous
spaces with connected or abelian stabilizer. J. Reine Angew. Math. 473 (1996), 181-194, DOI: https://doi.org/10.1515/crll.1995.473.181.</ref> Jointly with Cyril Demarche, he proved a similar result for the
Brauer-Manin obstruction to strong approximation<ref> Mikhail Borovoi and Cyril Demarche, Manin obstruction to strong
approximation for homogeneous spaces. [[Comment. Math. Helv.]] 88 (2013), no. 1, 1-54, DOI: https://doi.org/10.4171/CMH/277.</ref>
